the ice abundances in the low-mass protostellar sample are dominated by the CO freezeout phase and that the ice variations are dominated by the thermal and UV processing phase.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ice inventory is set during the prestellar phase, but that the exact ice abundances and their distribution are determined by the prestellar chemistry and the thermal and UV processing in protostellar envelopes.
the first ices form coevally, the second phase is dominated by CO-based chemistry and the last stage is dominated by thermal and UV processing.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the ice composition and the ice evolution from cores to protostars can be explained by a combination of hydrogenation, freezeout, and thermal and UV processing, with only a small contribution of the grain-surface chemistry.
